headline: High risk of prompt-injection, data leakage, and cascading errors from shared writable workspaces and broad egress; compliance risk is moderate.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Both agents can read and write files and use stdin/stdout, so a shared workspace or copied outputs can carry attacker-controlled instructions from LangGraph into Plandex. LangGraph’s graph nodes may ingest prior node outputs, and Plandex’s review-then-apply flow can still parse file content as trusted input. No explicit provenance isolation is documented.
conditions: IF the two agents share any writable directory or exchanged file artifact
IF Plandex reads LangGraph-generated text as task instructions without provenance tagging
mitigations: Separate the agents into distinct directories
Disable auto-apply in Plandex
Add a provenance header to every handoff file
Require manual review of any LangGraph-produced text before execution
requires-engineering: enforce content-type or schema validation on inter-agent messages

B_data_leakage.rationale: LangGraph handles model provider API keys and has broad network egress; Plandex also sends data to a cloud or self-hosted server and model provider. If they share a workspace, source code or graph state can flow from one agent into the other and then out to third parties. The pair touches sensitive application state and code by default.
conditions: IF either agent is pointed at the same project directory
IF Plandex is configured to use Plandex Cloud or any remote model provider
mitigations: Use separate workspaces for each agent
Remove secrets from shared files before handoff
Prefer self-hosted inference endpoints
Restrict network egress during review runs
requires-engineering: add redaction before any cross-agent export

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both agents have unrestricted filesystem write and shell execution, and both support multiple instances with shared state backends. LangGraph’s shared checkpointer store and Plandex’s server backend create a plausible concurrent-write path to the same mutable project artifacts, while Plandex can also modify git state. This matches the rubric’s dangerous overlapping-write pattern.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same repository or working tree
IF either backend stores shared state for the same task without locking
mitigations: Run the agents on separate branches
Disable concurrent writes to the same directory
Serialize edits through one coordinator
Pause one agent while the other applies changes
requires-engineering: add file-locking or transactional merge control

D_cascading_error.rationale: LangGraph is an orchestration framework whose node outputs can become downstream inputs, and Plandex is explicitly review-then-apply with optional auto-apply. That makes it plausible that LangGraph-generated text or facts are treated as authoritative by Plandex and then turned into code changes or shell actions without a verification step. The blast radius includes incorrect commits or destructive edits.
conditions: IF LangGraph output is fed directly into Plandex planning or apply steps
IF Plandex auto-apply is enabled or review is skipped
mitigations: Require human review before apply
Insert a verification step between agents
Disable auto-apply
Limit LangGraph to producing structured, schema-validated outputs
requires-engineering: add assertion checks before any git or shell action

E_compliance.rationale: Both profiles are docs-only and do not specify residency or retention guarantees, but both agents send data to external model providers or servers and handle secrets or source code. That creates a plausible retention and jurisdiction mismatch risk, though the profiles do not prove a specific regulated-data class like PHI or EU PII. Uncertainty pushes this above low.
conditions: IF regulated data is placed into either agent’s workspace
IF the remote provider or server retains prompts or files beyond the operator’s policy
mitigations: Avoid regulated data in shared runs
Use self-hosted endpoints where possible
Review retention settings before execution
Keep separate data domains per agent
requires-engineering: document residency and retention controls
